claims.text: A clinician note records a heart rate of 48 and states to hold metoprolol until the heart rate is reviewed on Thursday.

citations.quote: Heart rate 48. Hold metoprolol until the heart rate is reviewed on Thursday.

claims.text: Patient reports taking metoprolol every morning as usual and feeling fine.

citations.quote: I take metoprolol every morning as usual and feel fine.

claims.text: The record contains a conflicting medication fact for metoprolol: one entry says to hold it, while the patient-reported entry says it is still being taken.

citations.quote: Hold metoprolol until the heart rate is reviewed
I take metoprolol every morning as usual and feel fine.

open_questions: When was metoprolol first started, and what was the original dose?
Was the Thursday heart rate review carried out, and what did it show?
Did the clinician document a hold or restart of metoprolol after the heart rate was reviewed?
What were earlier recorded heart rates, and were there prior bradycardia episodes?
Who instructed the patient to continue taking metoprolol, and when was that documented?
Are there other medications affecting heart rate or blood pressure recorded earlier?
No allergies or reactions are recorded in the available entries; confirm allergy history with the patient.

citation.quote: I take metoprolol every morning as usual and feel fine.

candidate_highlights.risk_reason: Patient reports continuing metoprolol despite a clinician note holding it for a heart rate of 48.
candidate_highlights.suggested_action: Confirm with the patient and clinician whether metoprolol is currently being taken and reconcile the conflicting entries.
